description: Machine-readable Microsoft-to-Rust contract ledger. Suite defaults are deliberately conservative until individual source methods are reconciled with concrete Rust witnesses.

entries.notes: Fixed VT key-down vectors and the complete key-up VKEY range are portable Rust evidence. Microsoft default-character branches depend on MapVirtualKeyW, and non-KEY INPUT_RECORD dispatch belongs to the native boundary.

Rust covers all fifteen deterministic VT special-key modifier states, but the Microsoft source method also builds Windows keyboard state and observes active-layout ToUnicodeEx translation. The complete source contract therefore remains platform-owned rather than merely partially portable.
The portable Ctrl-Space and Ctrl-Alt-Space semantics are exact. Microsoft's additional NUL virtual-key lookup is produced by VkKeyScanExW under an explicitly selected Windows layout.

Rust directly covers the deterministic Backspace/Delete/Tab and slash/question outputs, but Microsoft derives part of the key identity through Windows keyboard-layout translation. The source method as a whole is therefore Partial, matching the later R08 functional audit.

Rust replays all 132 rows from Microsoft's KeyPressTests data source one-for-one, including the forced French Standard AZERTY layout, AltGr, locks, keypad PUA, modifier keys, media keys, F13-F24, event releases, alternate keys and associated text.

The Rust core exactly preserves the no-output result when KeyboardMapper reports the Windows dead-key translation as non-representable. Full equivalence remains platform-bound until the Windows ToUnicodeEx KeyboardMapper adapter is present.
The product presentation owner restores default cursor/attributes with no save and saves/restores TextAttribute together with the cursor state, matching both Microsoft cases.
DECTCEM mode 25 is now owned by the Rust presentation state and the witness exercises the complete starting-visible by ending-visible matrix.
An empty SGR is applied to the live Rust TextAttribute and resets all rendition and colors to defaults.
The Rust presentation owner applies Microsoft's complete single-parameter matrix, including rendition flags/resets, normal/default/bright foreground and background colors, and overline.
The parser-to-product path applies all four Microsoft subparameter vectors: curly underline, indexed foreground, indexed background, and indexed underline color.
Rust owns the complete rendition stack: full and nested push/pop plus Microsoft's selective intensity/background/double-underline and single/double/curly underline restoration cases.

Rust owns persistent TextAttribute intensity independently from foreground color selection: SGR 1 survives normal and 90-series color changes, 90-series colors do not enable intensity by themselves, and SGR 0 resets the state.
The live Rust response dispatch consumes DSR 5 and serializes the Microsoft operating-status response ESC[0n through the product response sink.
The live Rust response dispatch reads the active cursor and viewport, emits 1-based viewport-relative CPR, and preserves concatenated responses exactly as Microsoft expects.
The live Rust response dispatch emits DECXCPR from the active cursor/viewport plus the reported page identifier, including Microsoft's page 1 and page 3 vectors.
Private DSR 62 is routed through the live product aggregate and reports MacroBuffer space in exact 16-byte blocks after parser-driven DECDMAC definitions.
Private DSR 63 uses live MacroBuffer memory, preserves the request ID, and emits exact DCS checksum framing through the product sink.
Rust emits all eight Microsoft static private DSR responses exactly and preserves fail-closed sink behavior.
Primary DA is serialized from the live clipboard capability and matches both Microsoft capability vectors.
Secondary DA flows through the live response dispatch and emits the Microsoft DA2 response exactly.
Tertiary DA flows through the live response dispatch and emits the Microsoft DA3 DCS response exactly.
DECRQDE reads live geometry, horizontal pan, visible page and page-cursor coupling and serializes the exact response.
Both Microsoft permission values are serialized exactly through the live adapter response sink.
DECRQSS streams through the real DCS parser into live adapter state, covers Microsoft setting vectors, and preserves fallible sink behavior.
ANSI DECRQM reports Microsoft standard-mode set/reset states from owned or explicit report-only state.
The complete Microsoft private-mode request matrix reports exact set/reset state without swallowing platform side effects.
Permanent mode 2027 is owned as permanently enabled and reports DECRPM state 3 exactly after reset attempts.

DECRQCRA now flows parser-to-product through a real Rust TextBuffer checksum owner and fallible VT response sink, reproducing Microsoft's ASCII, Latin-1, rendition, protection, legacy-color, disabled/page-zero, and formatted-response vectors without hiding downstream display work.
The live ColorProductDispatch projects the canonical 267-slot ColorTableState and serializes Microsoft's complete DECCTR HLS and RGB tables exactly.
OSC 4 queries now resolve against the live color owner and reproduce all sixteen VT525 source responses with exact rgb:rrrr/gggg/bbbb framing.
Xterm resources 10/11/12 now resolve through live aliases and special color slots, including concatenation, INVALID_COLOR silence and unsupported-resource silence.
DECRQPSR format 2 now owns default eight-column stops, streamed DCS restore, sort/filter rules, width changes, clear-all, exact DCS report framing, and fail-closed product sink behavior in Rust.

DECRQPSR format 1 now serializes and restores live cursor/page state, rendition/protection flags, origin/SS2/SS3/delayed-wrap bits, locking shifts, 94/96 charset designations, and fail-closed sink behavior through the real Rust parser/product path.
DECCKM set/reset now flows through the product aggregate into the live Rust TerminalInput CursorKey mode; DECRQM observes the same owned state without leaving deferred adapter work.
Application/numeric keypad actions now flow from the parser through the product aggregate into the live Rust TerminalInput Keypad mode with no deferred adapter work.
The Adapter parser-control seam now mutates the live Rust StateMachine ANSI/VT52 mode directly, matching Microsoft's true-to-false SetAnsiMode observations without duplicating parser state.
ATT610 mode 12 now mutates the live final product cursor-blinking state for both Microsoft set/reset vectors, with DECRQM observing the same state.

The final product line-feed owner reuses the live TextBuffer, the same AdaptDispatchCore cursor, the live TerminalInput mode 20, and current erase attributes to reproduce all four Microsoft cursor-mutation cases without duplicate cursor state.
The final terminal-surface product owner stores the nonempty and empty Microsoft title values directly while the parser preserves all OSC title command variants.

All six Microsoft mouse tracking, encoding, and alternate-scroll modes now flow through the product aggregate into the live Rust TerminalInput owner; the existing R02 contracts separately prove emitted mouse encoding semantics.
All five Microsoft indexed foreground/background SGR vectors now flow through the real parser into the live Rust TextAttribute owner with exact 256-color indices.
Omitted/default extended-color parameters, partial RGB components, and out-of-range indexed/RGB values now match Microsoft against the live Rust TextAttribute owner.
Colon-delimited indexed/RGB subparameters, default components, color-space rejection, and out-of-range rejection now match Microsoft against the live Rust TextAttribute owner.
The canonical color owner now applies Microsoft RGB(1,2,3) across every palette index 0..255, proving concrete mutation over the full source domain.

Rust ports Microsoft's pure FontBuffer SetAttributes/_calculateDimensions algorithm and reproduces every source vector: matrix validation, explicit dimensions, 80/132 by 24/36/48 font sets, text/full-cell usage, and bitmap-driven sixel extent inference.

The Adapter parser-control seam now toggles the live AcceptC1 parser mode and reproduces Microsoft's ISO-2022/ISO-8859-1 versus UTF-8 code-page decision while preserving one canonical parser-mode owner.
DECAUPSS stores all Microsoft 94/96 character-set IDs through the live streamed DCS parser and product aggregate.
DECRQUPSS reads live assigned charset state, emits every Microsoft DCS response vector exactly, and preserves fallible product-sink behavior.

CSI macro invocation now executes synchronously back through the same live Rust StateMachine using an acyclic decorator seam. Default/maximum/out-of-range IDs, undefined macros, exact emitted text order, and Microsoft's strict recursive depth of sixteen are all witnessed against the canonical MacroBuffer.
Microsoft report function codes 18, 14, and 16 now flow parser-to-product against live Rust-owned text/cell/pixel geometry and serialize the exact ordered responses without deferred adapter work.
The terminal-surface product validates Microsoft's complete malformed matrix, parses replacement length and preserves the JSON remainder verbatim including embedded semicolons.
S7C1T/S8C1T now share the live TerminalInput mode and the final response owner converts CSI, DCS, OSC and ST framing exactly across Microsoft's secondary DA, tertiary DA and color-report vectors.
